children: Shares of HEG Advanced Materials (formerly known as HEG Ltd) surged nearly 15 per cent over the last three trading sessions, driven by potential gains from the company’s demerger and after winning a ₹218 crore order to supply lithium-ion battery banks to Indus Towers.
The company’s shares surged from ₹215 on September 17 (Thursday) to ₹248 on September 21 (Monday), a 15 per cent gain on NSE.
Last week, the company  announced that its subsidiary, Replus Engitech, received orders from Indus Towers to supply lithium-ion battery banks.
The order has to be fulfilled before March 31 next year, it said.

HEG’s shares have also benefited from the value-creation potential of its ongoing demerger, under which the graphite electrodes business will move into HEG Graphite which will subsequently be renamed HEG and taken forward as a separately listed, pure-play graphite electrodes company. The company is expected to be listed by the end of October.
The current listed company, HEG Advanced Materials retains the advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses.
Shareholders who held the shares on the record date of September 7 will receive one share in the graphite company for every one share held of HEG Advanced Materials.

Ravi Jhunjhunwala has been leading the graphite company as Chairman, MD and CEO from September 1, and will continue on the advanced materials company’s board in a non-executive capacity. Meanwhile, Riju Jhunjhunwala was appointed Chairman, MD and CEO of HEG Advanced Materials for a five-year term, subject to shareholder approval.

Riju Jhunjhunwala had earlier said that the demerger will create two focused, independently valued businesses, each with a clear strategy, disciplined capital allocation, and the flexibility to pursue its own growth path.
“We believe this sharper focus will enable each business to unlock its full potential while creating sustainable, long-term value for our shareholders,” he had said.

title: HEG Advanced Materials surges 15% in 3 sessions on ₹218 crore order win
